stories.headline: Knife Angel sculpture goes on display
stories.brief: A sculpture known as the Knife Angel is currently being exhibited. The artwork has been constructed using 100,000 knives that were previously seized by authorities. The piece is now available for public viewing.

stories.headline: Peterborough United manager monitors EFL developments
stories.brief: The manager of Peterborough United has been spotted observing Huddersfield Town’s recent rise to third place in the league standings. Meanwhile, a striker currently on loan from the Posh has successfully found the back of the net. Additionally, updates have been released regarding the latest progress in the EFL Trophy.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire curry house shortlisted for national award
stories.brief: A curry house based in Cambridgeshire has been named as a contender for a prestigious national prize. The restaurant is currently in the running for the top honour, according to reports from the Ely Standard. Further details regarding the specific name of the establishment or the nature of the award have not been disclosed.

stories.headline: Live facial recognition technology deployed in Cambridge
stories.brief: Police in Cambridge have begun using live facial recognition technology. The system is designed to help officers identify wanted individuals in public spaces. The rollout follows reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News regarding the implementation of this new surveillance method within the city. Residents and visitors to the area should be aware that this technology is now in operation.

stories.headline: Court of Appeal overturns solicitor fraud ruling
stories.brief: The Court of Appeal has overturned a previous legal ruling concerning a solicitor accused of ignoring fraud. The original decision had suggested the legal professional turned a "blind eye" to fraudulent activity. However, following the appeal, that finding has now been reversed. No further details regarding the identity of the solicitor or the specific nature of the case have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire roadwork delays drop following fines
stories.brief: New figures show a reduction in roadwork overruns across Cambridgeshire. The number of projects exceeding their planned duration has fallen by 42. This decrease follows the implementation of £424,000 in fines and charges issued to contractors. The data, reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, suggests that the financial penalties have been effective in encouraging works to be completed on schedule.

stories.headline: Long Sutton Neighbourhood Plan receives support
stories.brief: Long Sutton Parish Council has received backing for its neighbourhood plan. The move, reported by the Spalding South Holland News, marks a step forward in the local planning process for the area. No further details regarding the specific contents or the next stages of the plan have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Serious collision on the A142
stories.brief: A driver has been taken to hospital with serious injuries following a crash on the A142. Emergency services attended the scene of the incident. No further details regarding the circumstances of the collision or the current condition of the individual involved have been released at this time. Motorists are advised to remain aware of potential disruption in the area.

stories.headline: Robbie Savage comments on Peterborough United role
stories.brief: Robbie Savage has spoken about his position at Peterborough United. The former footballer has stated that he is prepared to prove his critics wrong in his new role at the club. No further details regarding his specific responsibilities or the nature of his appointment have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Plans submitted for final phase of East Cambridgeshire housing development
stories.brief: The Church Commissioners for England have submitted a planning application for the final stage of a major housing project in East Cambridgeshire. The proposal outlines the construction of 1,600 new homes as part of the community development.

stories.headline: East Cambridgeshire families encouraged to review household finances
stories.brief: Families living in East Cambridgeshire are being advised to review their current benefit entitlements and household bills. The recommendation comes as residents face ongoing increases in the cost of living. Local households are encouraged to check their financial circumstances to ensure they are receiving all the support available to them.

stories.headline: Peterborough parents patrol school crossing after safety concerns
stories.brief: Parents in Peterborough have begun patrolling a local school crossing themselves. The move follows a series of incidents at the site, prompting families to take action to ensure student safety. No further details regarding the specific nature of the incidents or the location of the crossing have been provided.

stories.headline: New bereavement centre opens in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A new facility for those experiencing bereavement has opened in East Cambridgeshire. The centre is situated by a lakeside, providing a dedicated space for support within the local community. Further details regarding the services offered at the site have not been provided.

stories.headline: Sponsorship deal provides boost for local football club
stories.brief: A football club in the region is reporting a renewed sense of pride following a new sponsorship agreement. The deal is expected to provide a significant boost to the club, according to reports from the Spalding South Holland News. Players have expressed positive sentiments regarding the partnership, which aims to support the team's ongoing development. Further details on the specific nature of the sponsorship have not been disclosed, but the club remains optimistic about the impact this investment will have on their future performance and local standing.

stories.headline: Historic steam train to visit Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A steam locomotive described as having a remarkable history is set to visit Cambridgeshire. Details regarding the specific train, the dates of its arrival, and its planned route through the county have not yet been confirmed. Residents and rail enthusiasts are advised to keep an eye on local updates for further information regarding the visit.

stories.headline: Arrangements underway to fill vacant councillor seats
stories.brief: Following the death of a local councillor, official procedures are now in place to fill the resulting vacancies. The South Holland News reports that arrangements are being made to appoint representatives to the seats left empty by the late official. Further details regarding the process or the specific wards affected have not yet been released. Residents are advised to monitor local council updates for information on how these positions will be filled.

stories.headline: BBC highlights historical significance of the Fens
stories.brief: The BBC has described the Fens as a location where the entirety of British prehistory is represented. The broadcaster highlighted the area's unique historical importance, suggesting that the landscape serves as a significant record of the nation's past.

stories.headline: Local diners name top Cambridgeshire pizza spots
stories.brief: A recent report from the Ely Standard has highlighted the best-rated pizza restaurants across Cambridgeshire. The rankings were compiled based on feedback and reviews provided by local diners in the area. Residents looking for recommendations on where to eat out can find the full list of popular venues on the Ely Standard website.

stories.headline: Charity badge to feature infamous March goose
stories.brief: A pin badge depicting a well-known goose from March is set to go on sale to raise money for charity. The bird, which gained a local reputation for its antisocial behaviour, will be immortalised on the new accessory. Details regarding which charity will benefit from the proceeds or when the pins will be available for purchase have not yet been confirmed.

stories.headline: Long Sutton care village staff receive award recognition
stories.brief: Staff at a care village in Long Sutton have been honoured at a recent awards ceremony. The team was recognised for their work in turning around the facility. Further details regarding the specific awards or the individuals involved have not been released.

stories.headline: Protest held against Cambridgeshire puppy breeding site
stories.brief: Hundreds of people have taken part in a demonstration against a puppy breeding facility in Cambridgeshire. The march was held to voice opposition to the site’s operations. No further details regarding the location or the specific organisers of the protest have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Peterborough school expansion plans approved
stories.brief: Peterborough’s cabinet has given the green light to a five point three eight million pound project to expand school facilities in the area. The investment aims to increase capacity within the local education system. Further details regarding which specific schools will benefit from the funding have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Five Cambridgeshire criminals convicted in September
stories.brief: A report from the Ely Standard confirms that five individuals were convicted of criminal offences across Cambridgeshire during the month of September. No further details regarding the specific identities of those involved or the nature of the crimes have been released at this time.

stories.headline: New play equipment installed at Westmead Avenue in Wisbech
stories.brief:
Children in Wisbech have a new place to play following a series of updates at the Westmead Avenue site. Fenland District Council has completed the renovations, which feature colourful equipment designed for youngsters aged between two and eight. 

Councillors Sidney Imafidon and Samantha Hoy visited the location this week to view the improvements. Work is now set to conclude with a final tidy-up of the area where the previous equipment was situated. The project is part of a wider programme of play area updates taking place across the district.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn man banned from driving for third time
stories.brief:
A 33-year-old man from King’s Lynn has been disqualified from driving for 40 months following a drink-driving incident. Anthony Purdy, of Gaskell Way, crashed his Ford Transit van into railings on Dairy Way in Gaywood on the evening of September 15. 

Police later attended his home address, where a breath test revealed he was more than double the legal alcohol limit. At Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Purdy pleaded guilty to drink-driving and failing to stop after a collision. In addition to the driving ban, he was fined £700 and ordered to pay further costs and surcharges. Magistrates declined to offer a rehabilitation course, noting this was the defendant's third disqualification for alcohol-related driving offences.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire launches pilot for AI crime reporting tool
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire has become the first area in the United Kingdom to trial a new artificial intelligence-powered tool for reporting crime. The technology is currently being piloted within the county to assist with the submission of reports. This initiative marks the first time such a system has been implemented in the UK.

stories.headline: Charity tea party held at Cambridgeshire care home
stories.brief: A care home in Cambridgeshire has hosted a tea party to raise money for charity. The event, reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, brought the local community together to support the fundraising effort. Further details regarding the specific charity supported or the total amount of money raised have not been disclosed.

stories.headline: Investigation follows death of young boy in water
stories.brief: A young boy has died following an emergency incident involving a child in water. Ambulance crews were called to the scene to provide urgent assistance, but the child could not be saved. No further details regarding the location or the circumstances of the incident have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Local football round-up: FA Cup progress and league updates
stories.brief: Spalding United have secured their place in the final qualifying round of the FA Cup. In other local football news, Deeping Rangers recorded a victory following a goal from Gash, while FC Peterborough delivered an impressive performance against the league leaders. Meanwhile, Peterborough Sports have provided an update regarding their new manager, following a continued strong run of form for the club.

stories.headline: Ely café supports volunteer in job search
stories.brief: A café in Ely is assisting a local volunteer as they work to build confidence for future employment. The initiative aims to help the individual, named Rayo, gain the necessary experience and self-assurance to secure a job. The project highlights the role of local businesses in supporting residents as they prepare for the workforce.

stories.headline: Looking back at local milestones in West Norfolk
stories.brief:
This week’s look back at local history highlights several notable events from past Octobers. In 2013, actor Tim Bentinck, known for his role in The Archers, officially opened the Hunstanton Heritage Centre. That same year, the Purfleet Trust in King’s Lynn secured a £114,000 lottery grant to support food bank users, while a misspelling on road signs at the Hardwick Industrial Estate was finally corrected.

Moving to 2017, King’s Lynn marked the 25th anniversary of the railway line’s electrification with a civic reception at the town hall. Other notable moments included the West Norfolk and King's Lynn Beekeepers Association celebrating their centenary and the unveiling of a new plaque at Downham Town Hall to preserve the history of its foundation stone.

stories.headline: Long-term lease secured for Ely Museum
stories.brief: Ely Museum has secured its future after signing a new 99-year lease. The agreement ensures the long-term stability of the site, allowing the museum to continue its operations in the city for the foreseeable future.

stories.headline: Two arrested following Lincolnshire police operation
stories.brief: Lincolnshire Police have arrested two people following an operation in the county. During the activity, officers seized a quantity of cash and a number of catalytic converters. Police also recovered a Bitcoin machine as part of the investigation. No further details regarding the individuals involved or the specific location of the seizures have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Looking back at local news from the archives
stories.brief:
We are taking a look back at stories from the archives. In October 1994, actress Liza Goddard visited a King’s Lynn bookstore to judge the Earthworm Children’s Book Award, joined by a giant mascot. 

Moving to 2013, campaigners working to save the King’s Arms pub in Shouldham extended their share deadline after raising £130,000 towards their £150,000 target. That same year, a new 61-metre wind turbine was constructed in North Lynn, while the True’s Yard Museum in King’s Lynn prepared to display rare photographs of aviator Amy Johnson’s crashed aircraft. These stories highlight just a few of the events that have shaped our local history over the years.

stories.headline: New glamping site proposed for Peterborough farm
stories.brief: A planning application has been submitted for a new glamping site located on a farm in Peterborough. The proposal, which was reported by the Peterborough Telegraph, outlines plans to develop the site for holiday accommodation. No further details regarding the scale of the project or a potential opening date have been released at this stage. Residents and interested parties can monitor the local planning portal for updates as the application progresses through the official review process.

stories.headline: Local court cases heard this week
stories.brief: A man who produced three indecent videos of a child is among those who appeared in court this week. The details were reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News. No further information regarding the identity of the individual or the specific outcome of the hearing has been released at this time.

stories.headline: Emergency services attend incident at Spalding park
stories.brief: Emergency crews, including an air ambulance, were called to a park in Spalding following reports that a man had been found not breathing. The incident prompted a significant response from 999 services. No further details regarding the man's condition or the circumstances surrounding the event have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire drug dealer sentenced for second time this year
stories.brief: A drug dealer has been handed a prison sentence for the second time in 2025. Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed the outcome, marking the second conviction for the individual within the current calendar year. No further details regarding the identity of the offender or the specific location of the crimes have been released by the police at this time.

stories.headline: South Wootton park wins top regional award
stories.brief:
Wootton Park has been named the best park in the Anglia In Bloom 2026 awards. The site beat 17 other entries to secure the gold trophy in the virtual category. The award was presented at a ceremony in St Ives to Will Border, chairperson of the Wootton Park Association. 

The park is managed by the association alongside the South and North Wootton parish councils. Mr Border praised the achievement, highlighting the hard work of the volunteers who maintain the grounds. The win saw the village park finish ahead of other notable locations, including The Walks and Tower Gardens in King's Lynn.

stories.headline: Campaign group considers cash rewards for information on child abusers
stories.brief: A campaign group led by a father is exploring the possibility of offering financial rewards for information regarding child abusers. The initiative is being developed as part of the organisation's latest project. Further details on how the scheme might operate have not yet been confirmed.

stories.headline: Crop fire reported in Whittlesey
stories.brief: Emergency services have responded to a large fire involving crops in the Whittlesey area. Reports indicate that the blaze was ignited following the explosion of a canister. No further details regarding the extent of the damage or any potential injuries have been released at this time. Residents are advised to remain aware of the situation as crews work at the scene.

stories.headline: Employment tribunal rejects unfair dismissal claim from former King’s Lynn head teacher
stories.brief:
An employment tribunal has dismissed a claim of unfair dismissal brought by Greg Hill, the former head teacher of Howard Junior School in Gaywood. Mr Hill, who served at the school from 2007 until his arrest in 2023, was dismissed by the Eastern Multi-Academy Trust in April 2024 following a conviction for harassment.

Judge KJ Palmer ruled there was no evidence to support Mr Hill’s claims of a conspiracy against him, describing his assertions as groundless. During the proceedings, the tribunal noted that Mr Hill failed to engage with the dismissal process and did not provide medical evidence to support his absence from the hearing. The judge also refused his request to reveal the identities of witnesses involved in the case.

stories.headline: Peterborough United appoint Robbie Savage as new manager
stories.brief: Peterborough United have confirmed the appointment of Robbie Savage as their new manager. The former professional player joins the club from his previous role as boss of Forest Green Rovers. The announcement follows reports from the BBC regarding the change in leadership at the club.

stories.headline: Major road closed following HGV collision
stories.brief: A major road in the region is currently closed to traffic following a collision involving a heavy goods vehicle. Emergency services are dealing with the incident, which has led to the route being shut. Motorists are advised to avoid the area and seek alternative routes while the closure remains in place. Further updates will be provided as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: National consultation begins for Mepal wind farm project
stories.brief: Plans for a proposed wind farm near Mepal have moved to the next stage. A national consultation process is now underway regarding the development. Residents and interested parties can now engage with the formal consultation phase as the project progresses.

stories.headline: Kent man fined after being found over alcohol limit in North Lynn
stories.brief:
A 23-year-old scaffolder from Kent has been fined after being found in charge of a vehicle while over the legal alcohol limit. Joshua Kurszewski, of Stangate Drive in Sittingbourne, was discovered by police on Crossbank Road in North Lynn on September 9 after a recovery worker raised concerns. A breath test revealed he was more than double the legal limit. 

Appearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court, Kurszewski admitted the offence. He was issued ten penalty points on his licence and ordered to pay a total of £645 in fines, surcharges, and costs. The court heard there was no evidence that he had been driving the vehicle at the time.

stories.headline: College of West Anglia students visit Houghton Hall exhibition
stories.brief:
Art and Design students from the College of West Anglia have visited Houghton Hall to study the work of British sculptor Lynn Chadwick. The Level 3 students viewed the artist’s distinctive figures as part of a project exploring the human form. 

During the trip, the group made observations and sketches of the sculptures within the historic landscape. Course director Mark Mann said the experience helped students engage with new creative ideas, while student Lola Hammond described the visit as an inspiring opportunity to view the artwork in its setting. The project encourages students to consider how scale and materials influence the way sculpture is experienced.

stories.headline: Speedway fans campaign for Local Plan protection
stories.brief: Supporters of the speedway are calling for the sport to be formally protected within the Local Plan. The campaign aims to secure the future of the activity through official planning policy. No further details regarding specific locations or proposed measures have been confirmed at this stage.

stories.headline: Man charged following incident involving teenager
stories.brief: A man is facing a criminal charge after being accused of attempting to incite a 14-year-old girl to engage in sexual activity. The case has been reported by the Spalding South Holland News. No further details regarding the identity of the accused or the location of the alleged incident have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over dust at Saxon Pit in Whittlesey
stories.brief: Questions have been raised regarding potential dust issues at the Saxon Pit site in Whittlesey. Reports indicate that concerns have been linked to the use of taxpayer funds in relation to the location. No further details have been provided regarding the specific nature of the dust fears or the financial claims involved.

stories.headline: Campaign launched to improve child road safety in the Fens
stories.brief:
A new road safety initiative, Be Bright Be Seen, is offering thousands of free reflective keyrings to schools, youth groups, and sports clubs across the region. Sponsored by Ashwood Homes, the campaign aims to increase the visibility of children as the nights draw in and the clocks go back on Sunday, October 25.

Organisers are encouraging the use of reflective gear and bright clothing to help pedestrians and cyclists stand out to motorists. This follows recent national data showing a rise in road traffic injuries. Local teachers, coaches, and youth leaders can apply for an allocation of the free keyrings by visiting the Fenland Citizen website.

stories.headline: Investigation launched following alleged assault at Cambridgeshire school
stories.brief: An investigation is underway following reports that a boy was assaulted at a school in Cambridgeshire. Authorities are currently looking into the incident, which was reported by the Ely Standard. No further details regarding the location of the school or the condition of the student have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Appeal for volunteers and donations to support Feed Fenland
stories.brief:
The Wisbech-based charity Feed Fenland is calling for community support to maintain its meal service for vulnerable residents. The organisation provides hot evening meals six nights a week at The Olive Academy on Coalwharf Road, often serving up to 200 portions per night. 

Operating without government or large-scale charity funding, the service relies entirely on donations and volunteers to cover costs, which average £80 per night. The charity is currently seeking more people to assist with cooking, serving, and general operations. Those interested in volunteering or providing financial support can contact the team via email at correspondence@feedfenland.com.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Dragon Festival returns next month
stories.brief:
The King’s Lynn Dragon Festival is set to return on Saturday, November 7, offering a variety of free family activities across the town. Cultural and heritage venues will host performances, trails, and medieval-themed entertainment between 10am and 3pm. 

Events include a dragon hunt, archery, and live shows at the Minster, alongside craft sessions at the local library. Several venues are participating, including the Lynn Museum, St George’s Guildhall, and True’s Yard. Free cinema screenings are also available at the Majestic and Corn Exchange, though tickets for these must be booked in advance. Residents are encouraged to check with individual venues, as some activities have limited capacity.

stories.headline: Robbie Savage named as new Peterborough United manager
stories.brief: Peterborough United have confirmed the appointment of Robbie Savage as their new manager. The news was reported earlier today by Sky Sports. No further details regarding the terms of the appointment or the club's upcoming fixtures have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Campaign launched against East Cambridgeshire wind farm plans
stories.brief: A new campaign has been established to oppose proposals for two wind farms in East Cambridgeshire. The development plans are currently facing resistance due to their proposed location on Grade 1 agricultural land. No further details regarding the specific sites or the groups involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Campaign launched against East Cambridgeshire wind farm plans
stories.brief: A new campaign has been launched to oppose the development of two proposed wind farms in East Cambridgeshire. The project has drawn criticism due to its planned location on Grade 1 agricultural land. Further details regarding the specific sites or the groups involved in the opposition have not yet been released. Residents are advised to monitor local planning updates as the situation develops.

stories.headline: Wisbech Furniture Warehouse to close and relocate
stories.brief:
Wisbech’s Furniture Warehouse is set to close its premises at the former Beales site on Church Terrace this weekend. The business, which moved into the building in 2023, says it is relocating to a nearby town to pursue better opportunities after the store space was significantly reduced. 

The owners have confirmed that no jobs will be lost as a result of the move. A final sale is currently underway, with the shop open from 10am until 8pm today and tomorrow. The location of the new premises has not yet been announced.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn mother urges residents to trust their instincts on health
stories.brief: A King’s Lynn mother is encouraging people to seek medical advice if they notice unusual changes in their health, even after receiving clear screening results. Emma Lambert, 49, was diagnosed with secondary breast cancer in 2024 after noticing discomfort, despite a recent clear mammogram. Following her diagnosis, she is supporting the ‘My Life, My Way’ campaign by the charity Make 2nds Count. The initiative aims to raise awareness of secondary breast cancer and highlight the importance of listening to your body. Ms. Lambert, who now focuses on local wellbeing activities, is sharing her story to ensure others understand the signs and know that support is available for those living with the condition.

stories.headline: Wisbech NHS Retirement Fellowship hosts harvest celebration
stories.brief:
The Wisbech branch of the NHS Retirement Fellowship held its annual harvest festival meeting this Wednesday at St Joseph’s Hall. Twenty-one members attended the event, which featured a lunch of jacket potatoes and salads, followed by homemade desserts. The afternoon included a programme of harvest-themed songs, poetry readings, and a raffle.

The group also began preparations for their October meeting, where members will learn to make Christmas candles with beekeeper Fiona Henderson. The fellowship meets on the final Wednesday of every month at 1.30 pm at the hall on Queens Road. New members are welcome to attend.

stories.headline: Nominations open for 2027 King’s Lynn and West Norfolk Mayor’s Business Awards
stories.brief:
Nominations are now being accepted for the 2027 King’s Lynn and West Norfolk Mayor’s Business Awards. Businesses have until 5pm on Friday, November 27, to submit entries across 11 different categories, including the Best Established Business of the Year.

The awards ceremony, now in its 38th year, is scheduled for Friday, March 5, 2027, at the Alive Corn Exchange in King’s Lynn. Organised by the Lynn News and Your Local Paper with support from West Norfolk Council, the event celebrates local commercial success and innovation. Judges will also select an overall Mayor’s Business of the Year from the category winners. Further details on how to enter are available through the event organisers.

stories.headline: National consultation begins for Mepal wind farm project
stories.brief: Plans for a new wind farm near Mepal have moved to the next stage of development. A national consultation process is now underway regarding the proposed site. Residents and interested parties can now engage with the formal planning process as the project advances.

stories.headline: Long Sutton waste company fined one million pounds
stories.brief: A waste management company based in Long Sutton has been ordered to pay one million pounds in fines. The penalty follows legal action taken against the firm for operating an illegal waste site. The case was reported by the Spalding South Holland News.

stories.headline: Capybara documentary to be screened in Wisbech this Sunday
stories.brief: A documentary exploring the global popularity of the capybara is coming to The Light cinema in Wisbech this Sunday. Titled The Route to Cappyness, the 99-minute film examines how the rodent became an international icon and a symbol of calm. Directed by Sharon Walia, the documentary features footage filmed across Brazil, Japan, the USA, and the UK. The film is rated U and is scheduled to begin at 5.35pm.

stories.headline: Terrington St Clement baby named Little Stars 2026 winner
stories.brief:
A four-month-old baby from Terrington St Clement has been crowned the winner of the 2026 Little Stars competition. Sonny Footer took the top spot following a public vote featuring 41 entrants. His family will receive a 20x16 inch canvas portrait as their prize.

The competition also saw one-year-old Pearl Barrett from South Wootton take second place, while two-year-old Freyja Norton from Feltwell finished third. Both families will also receive portrait prizes. Organisers say they will be in touch with the winners soon to arrange for the presentation of their photographs.

stories.headline: Three sentenced following Wisbech assault and false imprisonment
stories.brief:
Three people have been sentenced at Peterborough Crown Court following an incident in Wisbech on March 17. Two women were held against their will at a property on Waterlees Road and subjected to physical assaults. 

David Warden, 52, of Belt Drove in Elm, and 24-year-old Bricy Upton were each jailed for 30 months after admitting to two counts of false imprisonment. Warden was also sentenced for possession of heroin. Sharne Boon, 33, was ordered to complete 60 hours of unpaid work after admitting to two counts of assault. All three defendants have been issued with ten-year restraining orders, preventing them from contacting the victims.

stories.headline: Successful community fun day held at St Martha’s Primary in Gaywood
stories.brief:
St Martha’s Catholic Primary School in Gaywood has hosted its annual community fun day. The event featured a variety of activities, including fairground rides, games, and live performances from local talent, a Ju-Jitsu champion, and the King’s Lynn theatre company, KLODS. 

Attendees enjoyed food provided by the local Malayali community, who also donated £660 to the school council from their sales. Raffle winners at the event took home prizes including a Nintendo Switch and a 55-inch television. Organisers have thanked the staff, volunteers, and local businesses who supported the day, describing the occasion as a success that was filled with laughter from start to finish.

stories.headline: Robbie Savage named as new Peterborough United manager
stories.brief: Peterborough United have announced the appointment of Robbie Savage as their new manager. The club confirmed the news today, marking a significant change in leadership for the Posh. Fans across the Fens will be watching closely to see how the team performs under his guidance as the season progresses.

stories.headline: New Joy Bistro opens in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: An award-winning café owner has expanded their business in East Cambridgeshire. A second branch of Joy Bistro has officially opened its doors within the local area. This marks the latest venture for the proprietor, who already operates an established café site. Residents looking for new dining options can now visit the second location, which is currently welcoming customers in the village.

stories.headline: Fatal collision on A17 at Sutton Bridge
stories.brief: A driver has died following a collision on the A17 at the Sutton Bridge swing bridge. Emergency services were called to the scene of the incident. No further details regarding the circumstances of the collision or the identity of the individual involved have been released at this time. Motorists are advised to check for any ongoing travel disruption in the area.

stories.headline: Health study results due for Whittlesey pit site
stories.brief: Findings from a health study concerning the controversial pit site in Whittlesey are set to be released. The report, which examines the site that has been the subject of local debate, will be made public following the completion of the investigation. Residents across the Fens are awaiting the publication of these results to understand the potential health implications associated with the location. Further details regarding the study's conclusions are expected to follow once the information is officially published.

stories.headline: Fire crews tackle blaze in Elm
stories.brief:
Firefighters from six stations were called to Nettle Bank in Elm yesterday afternoon following reports of a fire. Crews from Wisbech, March, Chatteris, Outwell, Thorney and Ramsey arrived at 4:33pm to find a large bonfire spreading towards a nearby building. 

Wearing breathing apparatus, teams used hose reels and jets to extinguish the flames and prevent further damage. Firefighters remained on the scene until 9:15pm and have since conducted regular inspections to ensure the area is safe. Officials have confirmed the cause of the fire was accidental.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn man honoured for charity work in Indonesia
stories.brief:
A King’s Lynn man has received national recognition for his efforts to support communities in Indonesia. Samuel Oakes was highly commended in the international impact category at the inaugural University of Worcester Alumni Awards. 

Mr Oakes, an outdoor adventure leadership and management graduate, founded the UK-registered charity ATOVA International. His work focuses on education, youth development, and health. Through the charity, he has helped secure over £100,000 in funding for sustainable community programmes. Mr Oakes, who has spent the last decade living alongside the communities he serves, described the award as a surreal moment after years of working away from home.

stories.headline: Fenland residents invited to share views on dog control rules
stories.brief:
Fenland District Council is seeking public feedback on proposals to extend dog control regulations across the region. The current Public Spaces Protection Order, which mandates rules such as keeping dogs on leads in cemeteries and fenced play areas, is due to expire this December. 

The consultation, which began on September 11, asks residents for their views on extending these measures for another three years until December 2029, alongside potential minor adjustments. You have until October 9 to submit your response. Feedback will be presented to cabinet members in November to help decide whether to extend, amend, or end the order. Full details are available on the Fenland District Council website.

stories.headline: Over 10,000 sign petition to support Queen Elizabeth Hospital
stories.brief:
A campaign to protect vital services at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has reached a significant milestone, with more than 10,000 people signing a petition. Liberal Democrat Rob Colwell, who is leading the initiative, thanked the public for their support in safeguarding local emergency and hospital care.

Supporters are now being invited to take part in a demonstration at the Tuesday Market Place on October 17. Participants are asked to gather at 11:30 am for a "Human A&E queue" event. Attendees are encouraged to bring a sign displaying their home town or village and their travel time to the hospital, as the QEH Community Action Group prepares to submit the petition.

stories.headline: Peterborough City Council updates flood risk policy for new builds
stories.brief: Peterborough City Council has announced new measures regarding flood risk management for upcoming property developments. The local authority is implementing updated guidelines to ensure that new construction projects across the area properly account for potential flooding. These changes are designed to address environmental safety standards for future housing and commercial sites within the city’s jurisdiction. Residents and developers are advised to consult the council’s official planning documentation for further details on how these updated requirements may affect new building applications moving forward.

stories.headline: Council to oppose asylum seeker housing plan in Fenland village
stories.brief: Local authorities have announced they will robustly challenge a proposal to accommodate 26 asylum seekers within a Fenland village. The council confirmed its intention to fight the plans, though further details regarding the specific location or the timeline for the development have not been released. Residents are advised that the council is taking formal steps to oppose the scheme. We will bring you more information on this story as it becomes available.

stories.headline: Roadworks scheduled for A17
stories.brief: Drivers in the Fens should prepare for disruption on the A17 starting this Wednesday. Roadworks are set to take place at three specific locations along the route, affecting Saracen's Head, Sutterton, and Long Sutton. Motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and allow extra time for travel through these areas while the work is carried out.

stories.headline: Plans proposed for large wind turbines on farmland
stories.brief: New proposals have been put forward to construct large-scale wind turbines on agricultural land. According to reports, the project would see the installation of what have been described as gargantuan turbines in the countryside. Further details regarding the specific locations or the scale of the development have not yet been confirmed. Residents are advised to monitor local planning portals for updates as the application process continues.

stories.headline: Wisbech to host Volunteer and Community Fair next month
stories.brief:
Residents in Wisbech are invited to attend a Volunteer and Community Fair taking place next month. The free event will be held at the Queen Mary Centre on Queens Road on Saturday, November 14, between 10am and 1pm. 

Organised by the Fenland team from Volunteer Cambs, the fair offers a chance to meet local groups seeking support. The day will also feature a craft fair hosted by The Ferry Project, alongside family activities provided by Fenland Family Volunteering. Those interested in learning more about local opportunities can visit the event or email info@volunteercambs.org.uk for further details.

stories.headline: Plans unveiled for £13 million King’s Lynn development
stories.brief:
Proposals have been revealed for a new £13 million retail development near the Jubilee roundabout in King’s Lynn. Developer Rothstone is working on plans for a site south of Beveridge Way, which would feature an Aldi supermarket, an EG petrol station, and a Starbucks drive-thru. The project is expected to create up to 80 full and part-time jobs.

A public consultation on the scheme is now open and will run until Monday, October 12. Residents can share their views on the proposals online, by phone, or by post before a formal planning application is submitted. Further details on how to provide feedback are available through the project’s consultation team.

stories.headline: Lorry overturns near Soham
stories.brief: A lorry has overturned on a road near Soham. Images from the scene show the vehicle on its side following the incident. Motorists travelling in the area are advised to take care as emergency services deal with the aftermath. No further details regarding the cause of the incident or any potential injuries have been released at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn care homes raise over £500 for Macmillan Cancer Support
stories.brief:
Two care homes in King’s Lynn have raised £514.50 for Macmillan Cancer Support following a joint charity coffee morning. Amberley Hall and Goodwins Hall hosted the event at the Gaywood Church Rooms last Friday, September 25. 

The gathering was attended by residents, members of the public, and the Mayor of West Norfolk, Steve Bearshaw, who was joined by his wife, Marisol. Guests were entertained with live music from singer Emily Blake throughout the morning. Organisers have described the fundraising effort as a success.

stories.headline: Winvic selected for Cambridgeshire road repair trial
stories.brief: Construction firm Winvic has been awarded a contract to lead an innovative road repair trial in Cambridgeshire. The project, reported by Highways News, will see the company test new methods for maintaining the county's highway network. Further details regarding the specific locations or the nature of the repair techniques involved in the trial have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Protest planned in Leverington over asylum seeker hostel proposal
stories.brief:
A peaceful protest is scheduled for this Sunday in Leverington regarding government plans to use Roman Court as a hostel for asylum seekers. Organised by Reform county councillor Chris Tirrell, the gathering will begin at noon at Troughton Way. The proposal aims to house 26 women and children at the site, as part of a wider plan to accommodate 205 asylum seekers across the Fenland district. 

Both the local district council and MP Steve Barclay have expressed opposition to the move. A final decision on the future of the Roman Court site is expected from the government by October 16.

stories.headline: Police appeal for witnesses following King's Lynn collision
stories.brief:
Police are appealing for information following a collision at the Southgates roundabout in King's Lynn last Thursday morning. The incident occurred shortly before 6:30am and involved a white BMW and a motorbike. The motorcyclist was taken to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital with a broken wrist and ankle injuries.

A man in his 40s was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving and driving while disqualified. He has been released on bail until November 24 while investigations continue. Officers are asking anyone with dashcam footage from the area at the time of the collision to come forward.

stories.headline: Ely man jailed for arson at his own home
stories.brief: A man from Ely has been sentenced to time in prison after starting a fire at his own property. The case, reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, confirms that the individual was convicted of arson. No further details regarding the date of the incident or the length of the custodial sentence have been provided.

stories.headline: Investigation launched following alleged assault at Cambridgeshire school
stories.brief: An investigation is underway following reports of an assault involving a boy at a school in Cambridgeshire. Details regarding the incident remain limited at this stage, but authorities have confirmed that inquiries are currently being carried out. No further information has been released regarding the condition of the student or the specific location of the school involved. We will bring you more updates as they become available.

stories.headline: Record attendance at King’s Lynn and West Norfolk Law Society ball
stories.brief: The King’s Lynn and West Norfolk Law Society held its annual celebration ball at the town’s historic town hall on Friday, September 11. The event, which serves as a key date in the society’s calendar, saw one of its highest attendances in recent years. Legal professionals and members of the local business community gathered for an evening that included a formal dinner, live music from the Soul Sisters, and a speech by Judge Simon Spence. Society president Joshua Shuardson-Hipkin thanked those who attended and the committee for their work in organising the event. The evening was supported by several sponsors, including headline sponsor Cynergy Bank.

stories.headline: Peterborough United managerial appointment delayed
stories.brief: The appointment of Robbie Savage as the new manager of Peterborough United is currently on hold. Reports indicate that the delay is due to an ongoing dispute regarding compensation. No further details have been released regarding when the situation might be resolved or when a final decision is expected.

stories.headline: Campaign launched against East Cambridgeshire wind farm proposals
stories.brief: A new campaign has been established to oppose plans for two wind farms in East Cambridgeshire. The proposed developments are located on Grade 1 agricultural land. No further details regarding the specific locations or the groups involved in the opposition have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Campaign launched against East Cambridgeshire wind farm plans
stories.brief: A new campaign has been established to oppose proposals for two wind farms in East Cambridgeshire. The development plans have drawn criticism due to their proposed location on Grade 1 agricultural land. Further details regarding the specific sites or the groups involved in the opposition have not yet been released.

stories.headline: New craft hub to open on King’s Lynn High Street this weekend
stories.brief:
A new craft hub, Pia’s Place, is set to open on King’s Lynn High Street this weekend. Owned by Gaywood resident Pia Cawston, the shop will offer a variety of creative workshops, including basket weaving, watercolour painting, and children’s activities. The venue also features a selection of vintage items alongside coffee and homemade cake.

The doors open to the public this Saturday from 9am until 3pm, and Sunday from 10am until 4pm. Following the launch, the shop will operate from Wednesday to Sunday, between 9am and 4pm. The owner describes the new venture as a space for all ages to enjoy.

stories.headline: Plans submitted for new East Cambridgeshire wind farm
stories.brief: A new wind farm project has been proposed for East Cambridgeshire. According to reports, the development has the potential to generate enough electricity to power more than 200,000 homes. Further details regarding the specific location and timeline for the construction have not yet been confirmed.

stories.headline: Former Springwood student begins studies at Cambridge
stories.brief:
A former student from Springwood High School in King’s Lynn has begun her university career at Cambridge. Eva Kalabina, who achieved three A* grades and one A in her A-Levels, is now studying Economics, Law, and Environment. 

The 18-year-old credited the support of her teachers at the West Norfolk Academies Trust school for helping her secure her place. Looking ahead, Ms. Kalabina hopes to pursue a career within the technology industry or consultancy. She described her time at the Lynn school as a positive experience that helped her grow both academically and personally.

stories.headline: Emergency lock closures leave boaters stranded in March
stories.brief: Boaters are currently unable to move through March following the introduction of emergency lock closures. The restrictions have left vessels marooned in the area. No further details regarding the cause of the closures or when the locks might reopen have been provided. Those planning to travel through the town by water are advised to be aware of the ongoing disruption.

stories.headline: Top ratings for West Norfolk leisure centres
stories.brief:
Four council-run leisure centres in West Norfolk have been awarded a ‘very good’ rating following a national quality assessment. The sites, managed by Alive West Norfolk, include Lynnsport and St James’ Pool in King’s Lynn, Downham Leisure, and The Oasis in Hunstanton. 

The Quest for Facilities scheme evaluated the centres through mystery visits and independent inspections, focusing on areas such as customer service, safety, and community engagement. In addition to this rating, the service has also received The Active Standard certification from the trade body ukactive. Council officials have praised the staff for their ongoing commitment to maintaining high standards across all four facilities.

stories.headline: Red Arrows to fly over Cambridgeshire this week
stories.brief: Residents across Cambridgeshire are being advised that the Red Arrows are scheduled to fly over the county this week. The display team will be visible from various locations, though specific flight paths and timings have not been confirmed in this report. Those hoping to catch a glimpse of the aircraft are encouraged to keep an eye on the skies throughout the coming days. Further details regarding the exact route and viewing opportunities are expected to be available through local news sources as the week progresses.

stories.headline: Women's football team to face Peterborough United in League Cup
stories.brief: The women's football team is set to host Peterborough United in the opening round of the League Cup. The fixture was confirmed following the latest draw. Fans are now looking ahead to the upcoming match as the side prepares for this first-round encounter.

stories.headline: Long-term lease secured for Ely Museum
stories.brief: Ely Museum has confirmed it will remain at the Old Gaol site for the next century. The institution has successfully secured a new lease agreement that runs until the year 2125. The museum, which is housed in the historic building, will continue to operate from the premises for the foreseeable future.
